source.title: MimicNorm: Weight Mean and Last BN Layer Mimic the Dynamic of Batch Normalization
source.authors: Fei Wen; Wen-Rui Dai; Cheng-Lin Li; Jun-Ni Zou; H. Xiong

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training outcomes for normalization and initialization changes, bearing on V3, V5, and V6 using a different recipe from the original studies. Its empirical comparisons are aimed at convergence and training behavior.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own CIFAR-100 and ImageNet training results, learning-rate sweep, and stated training failures. NTK derivations and cited results are not empirical rows. Figure-only training curves are not converted into numeric values.
record.test_reason: The learning-rate sweep and normalization ablations test V6: accuracy within ten epochs measures speed of accuracy gain, and explicit divergence comparisons measure learning-rate tolerance. No experiment measures V5's stability threshold, curvature, or catapult dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, MimicNorm replaces intermediate BN layers with weight mean, modified initialization and residual scalars while retaining a final BN layer. The authors report broadly comparable accuracy and reduced memory, early training acceleration from weight mean, and larger-learning-rate stability from the final BN layer. They also acknowledge slightly lower ShuffleNetV2 ImageNet accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: MimicNorm uses mean subtraction on convolutional weights, modified initialization, residual-branch scalar multipliers, and a final BN layer; the paper compares it with BN networks and Fixup.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by method and learning rate. VGG16 may diverge with learning rate 0.1; NoNorm and weight mean perform poorly at larger rates in the first 10 epochs, while the final BN layer supports training at larger rates. ShuffleNetV2 ImageNet uses a modified training strategy and MimicNorm slightly underperforms BN.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 1 and 3 compare final test accuracy, including lower Fixup accuracy and broadly comparable MimicNorm accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MimicNorm generally preserves final predictive accuracy while reducing memory consumption relative to BN in the tested architectures.

record.problems: The experiments report accuracy and memory rather than training classification error. Training-curve values are shown in figures without extracted numeric values. Table 2 reports accuracy only. The paper says its ImageNet ShuffleNetV2 results use a modified training strategy.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 memory entries were omitted because memory consumption is not a measure in the claim versions. Table 2 entries for learning rates 0.02, 0.05, 0.5, and 1.0 were omitted because they report only accuracy and do not show the named behaviors; Figure 6 and Figure 7 training curves were not assigned numeric values because figure-only values are not legible as exact text results. Fixup comparison results remain in rows where the tables report them.

untested.parts: No zero or near-zero training classification error result, label-corruption experiment, or relevant model-size comparison.
No two-layer teacher-student optimization or extra-neuron comparison.
No controlled plain-versus-residual depth degradation experiment, very deep tanh training, or residual depth sweep without normalization.

No isolated test of activation-matched initialization improving training speed or trainable depth; no orthogonal-versus-Gaussian or 10,000-layer experiment. Weight mean is an ongoing operation bundled with modified initialization.
All parts: no initial linearized stability limit, curvature trajectory, squared-loss catapult experiment, or full-batch edge-of-stability measurement.

The original sigmoid-MNIST, VGG-CIFAR-10 and Inception-ImageNet settings are not reproduced. Final test accuracies do not establish equivalent Fixup training speed; no quantitative time-to-accuracy comparison is extracted.

missing.what: Separate convergence-stability outcomes for NoNorm VGG16 and Fixup ResNet50: both asterisked entries mean unstable training with occasional failure to converge. The record incorrectly says the asterisk is unexplained.
missing.locator: Table 1 footnote and accompanying CIFAR-100 discussion; accuracy rows R6 and R11

record.verdict_notes: Accuracy measured within a fixed early training budget is relevant to V6's speed claim; final test accuracy alone is not. The omitted Figure 6–7 curves and additional Table 2 learning rates are already declared in rows_left_out. MimicNorm retains normalization, so its success does not demonstrate training entirely without normalization. No verdict depends on cited results or exact numerical readings of plotted curves.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label or corrupted-label experiment, and no comparison of model size or training duration against training classification error.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or sweep over teacher/student neuron counts.
Compares normalization and initialization methods but does not test plain batch-normalized networks against identity-shortcut networks for training error as stated in V3.

Does not compare orthogonal and Gaussian initializations or test trainable depth as specified. Weight-mean initialization and its training curves are not the activation-matched or orthogonal initialization comparison named in this version.
No squared-loss wide-network experiment or measurement of curvature/sharpness relative to a stability threshold.
No sigmoid MNIST or VGG CIFAR-10 experiment; no Fixup recipe with its scalar biases and multipliers as a test of equivalent speed and stability without normalization.
